title: Freshwater Farm Plan (Canterbury, with Schedule 7)
description: Freshwater Farm Plan (Canterbury, with Schedule 7) (Canterbury (LWRP Schedule 7 kept)), draft as at 2026-10-30. RCL platform template (draft, Claude research agent 30 Oct 2026); needs Josh's content approval (PLANS.md §11). Sources: [FR] Resource Management (Freshwater Farm Plans) Regulations 2023 (SL 2023/113), version as at 26 May 2026 <https://www.legislation.govt.nz/secondary-legislation/pco-drafted/2023/113/en/latest/>; [RMA217E] Resource Management Act 1991 s 217E (as amended 21 August 2025) <https://mail.nzlii.org/nz/legis/consol_act/rma1991200/s217e.html>; [S7a] Canterbury Land and Water Regional Plan, Schedule 7 Farm Environment Plan (printed pp. 435-440), copy hosted by MHV Water <https://mhvwater.nz/images/Schedule_7_LWRP.pdf>; [S7b] Schedule 7 Farm Environment Plan - PC 5 (copy hosted by MHV Water) <https://www.mhvwater.nz/images/Schedule_7_Farm_Environment_Plan.pdf>; [LWRP] Canterbury Land and Water Regional Plan (operative, incl. PC7 from 10 March 2025) <https://www.ecan.govt.nz/your-region/plans-strategies-and-bylaws/canterbury-land-and-water-regional-plan/canterbury-land-and-water-regional-plan>; [ECANAUD] ECan: Information for auditors (Certified FEP Auditor Manual, November 2022) <https://www.ecan.govt.nz/your-region/farmers-hub/farming-plans-and-consenting/farm-environment-plans/information-for-auditors>; [PAC] HDLG/ECan FEP pre-audit check form (two versions, sprint drops) (sprint drop, not in the repository). Before publishing: Objective and target wording is from a secondary copy of LWRP Schedule 7 [S7a]; ECan's operative consolidated plan was not reachable from the sandbox. Plan Change 7 (operative 10 March 2025) amended Schedule 7 (springs added as a receptor; Waimakariri and OTOP nitrogen-reduction additions). Read the operative Schedule 7, correct any wording (notably 5E, which may now name springs), fill cant.s7.sub.waimakariri and cant.s7.sub.otop from it, then publish v2 with this flag removed. Part C sets the auditor and audit criteria only. Grades A-D and audit frequency come from the Certified FEP Auditor Manual (Nov 2022) and consent conditions, not from Schedule 7. Proposed fact types named in binds (risk_significance, fep_audit_grade, fep_audit_loc) do not exist yet; PL8/PL10 add them or bind elsewhere. Part 9A of the RMA has never been applied to Canterbury by Order in Council, so no Canterbury farm has a legal freshwater farm plan duty today; ECan says FEP obligations continue under consents and rules (27 Jan 2026). Crosswalk from fep-cant-s7 v1: Schedule 7 nodes carry unchanged; new input needed for cant.catchment.ecan_cccv, cant.catchment.ngai_tahu, cant.catchment.zone, cant.catchment.zone_outcomes, cant.map.regional_zones, cant.records.fep_history, nz.admin.reliance, nz.catchment.context, nz.catchment.plan_provisions, nz.catchment.regard, nz.catchment.tangata_whenua, nz.map.actions, nz.map.catchment, nz.records.audit, nz.records.certification, nz.records.evidence, nz.risk.method; no longer used: cant.s7.plan.meta.route, cant.s7.plan.meta.approved_template, cant.s7.plan.summary.vision, cant.s7.plan.summary.farm_story, cant.s7.lmu.unit.land_use.

cant.s7.plan.meta.transform: fields: prepared_by -> preparer_name; organisation -> organisation; prepared_on -> prepared_on; version_label -> version_label | route and approved_template are no longer used (the FWFP replaces the Part A route choice)

cant.s7.plan.summary.transform: fields: summary -> overview | vision and farm_story are not carried (no FWFP node); kept in the FEP issue

cant.s7.property.owner.transform: also to nz.admin.other_parties | fields: owner_name -> nz.admin.operator.operator_name; lessee_name -> nz.admin.other_parties.name | a person confirms who the farm operator is (the person with final responsibility; may be the lessee); a lessee becomes an other-parties row with role Leaseholder; contact_phone and contact_email come from cant.s7.property.contact; nzbn needs new input

cant.s7.property.legal.transform: fields: parcel -> parcel; title_ref -> title_ref; tenure -> tenure | title_ref needs input where the FEP gave only a legal description

cant.s7.property.areas.transform: also to nz.admin.land_use | fields: total_area_ha -> nz.admin.areas.total_area_ha; effective_area_ha -> nz.admin.areas.effective_area_ha; leased_area_ha -> nz.admin.areas.leased_area_ha; land_use -> nz.admin.land_use.land_use; stock_summary -> nz.admin.land_use.stock_summary | irrigated_area_ha and winter_grazing_ha stay as facts (bound) and feed the irrigation and winter grazing map layers

cant.s7.consents.transform: fields: consent_number -> consent_number; consent_type -> consent_type; purpose -> purpose; status -> status; expires_on -> expires_on

cant.s7.map.property.transform: also to nz.map.farming_features, cant.s7.map.extra | layers: boundary -> nz.map.vulnerabilities.boundary; land_units -> nz.map.vulnerabilities.land_units; water -> nz.map.vulnerabilities.natural_water; csa -> nz.map.vulnerabilities.csa; riparian_vegetation -> cant.s7.map.extra.riparian_vegetation; stock_access -> cant.s7.map.extra.stock_access; sig_biodiversity -> cant.s7.map.extra.sig_biodiversity; hrrpz -> cant.s7.map.extra.hrrpz; flood_assets -> cant.s7.map.extra.flood_assets; access_routes -> cant.s7.map.extra.access_routes | Schedule 7 'water' splits into natural and artificial waterbodies: a person assigns drains and ponds to artificial_water

cant.s7.lmu.unit.transform: fields: code -> code; name -> name; area_ha -> area_ha; description -> description; soils -> soils; irrigated -> irrigated | land_use is not carried; drained needs input

cant.s7.lmu.vulnerability.transform: fields: waterlogging -> waterlogging; p_sediment_runoff -> p_sediment_runoff; n_leaching -> n_leaching; structural -> structural; erosion -> erosion; other -> other | blank or 'Not stated' values become new input because the four core vulnerabilities are required in the FWFP

cant.s7.risk.assessment.transform: also to nz.risk.activity | fields: risk_label -> nz.risk.significance.risk_label; land_unit -> nz.risk.significance.land_unit; significance -> nz.risk.significance.significance; management_area -> nz.risk.significance.management_area; activity -> nz.risk.activity.activities | each rating pre-fills as the FEP author's prior assessment (assessed_by = FEP preparer, assessed_on = FEP date), shown for the new assessor to confirm or replace; Schedule 7 management areas map to activity groups: Nutrients->Nutrients, Irrigation->Irrigation, Cultivation and soil structure->Land and soil, Animal effluent->Animal effluent, Waterbodies->Waterways and wetlands, Point sources->Point sources, Water use->Other farming activity

cant.s7.actions.transform: fields: action -> action; land_units -> land_units; timeframe -> timeframe; due_on -> due_on; existing_or_new -> existing_or_new; category -> category; target_ref -> s7_target; records -> records; management_area -> management_area | management_area maps as for the risk assessment; category carries when the FEP gave Regulated/Catchment/Supplementary, otherwise new input; risk_addressed and activity are new input unless the FEP row had them; existing_or_new defaults to Existing for actions marked done

parts.title: About this plan and the farm
parts.guidance: The basic facts about who runs the farm, where it is and what consents it holds. A certifier checks every item here, so leave nothing blank: write 'none' where something does not apply.

nodes.title: Farm operator
nodes.guidance: The farm operator is the person or business with final responsibility for running the farm (often the owner, sometimes a lessee or sharemilker company). Give the NZ Business Number if the business has one.

nodes.title: Other owners, leaseholders and licence holders
nodes.guidance: Anyone else who owns, leases or holds a licence over land in this farm. Add a row for each. Needed when anyone other than the operator owns, leases or licenses land in the farm.

nodes.title: Plan prepared by
nodes.guidance: Who wrote this plan and when. If you wrote it yourself, put your own name.

nodes.title: Physical address
nodes.guidance: The farm's road address (the one a certifier or auditor would drive to).

nodes.title: Land titles and parcels
nodes.guidance: Every record of title and legal parcel the farm is made up of, including leased or licensed land. Copy them from LINZ titles.

nodes.title: Farm area
nodes.guidance: Total area of the farm in hectares, and how much of it is leased or licensed.

nodes.title: Land use
nodes.guidance: What the farm is used for, e.g. 'Sheep and beef with dairy grazing' or 'Dairy, 450 cows'. List each land use if there are several.

nodes.title: Current resource consents
nodes.guidance: Each current resource consent that relates to farming on this land: water takes, discharges, land use. Give the consent number as the council writes it. Schedule 7: list every ECan consent held for the property, not only those about farming effects.

nodes.title: Other rules this plan is used to meet
nodes.guidance: If a rule or national standard lets a certified farm plan stand in for another requirement (for example the stock exclusion or winter grazing rules), and you intend to rely on that, name the requirement here. Needed when the operator intends to rely on the certified plan to meet another requirement.

fields.label: Rule or regulation it comes from

parts.title: Land units and their inherent vulnerabilities
parts.guidance: Split the farm into land units: areas with similar soils, slope and drainage. For each one say how naturally vulnerable it is to losing contaminants to water, before thinking about how it is farmed.

nodes.title: Land unit
nodes.guidance: Give the land unit a short code and name (LU1 - Irrigated light soils), its area, and a description of its soils, slope, drainage and whether it is irrigated. A land unit can be in more than one piece.

nodes.title: Inherent vulnerabilities
nodes.guidance: How vulnerable this land unit is, by nature, to each pathway. Use the same scale for every land unit. Add anything else that matters here, such as erosion-prone slopes or a high water table.

parts.title: Catchment context, challenges and values
parts.guidance: What the regional council says matters in your catchment: the state of its water, what tangata whenua value, and the plan objectives that apply. Your plan has to show it has taken this into account. If the council has not published this information yet, say so.

nodes.title: The catchment and its water
nodes.guidance: Name the catchment or freshwater management unit and summarise the condition of its rivers, lakes, wetlands and groundwater, and the main contaminants of concern downstream of the farm.

fields.label: Council has published catchment context information
Where water from the farm ends up

nodes.title: Tangata whenua values
nodes.guidance: Values, sites and species important to tangata whenua in the catchment, including traditional names for waterbodies, from the council's information and any iwi management plan lodged with the council. Needed when council catchment context information is available.

nodes.title: Plan objectives and limits that apply
nodes.guidance: The regional plan objectives, limits and any council action plan that apply to this catchment.

nodes.title: How this plan responds
nodes.guidance: In a few sentences, how your actions respond to the catchment's challenges (for example: 'fencing and planting the stream reduces sediment, the catchment's main issue'). Actions that respond directly to catchment values are 'Catchment' actions in the action plan.

fields.label: How the plan has regard to the catchment

parts.title: Farming activities and risks to freshwater
parts.guidance: For each activity on the farm, what could go wrong for water and how serious it is on each land unit. Forestry, packhouses and processing sites, houses and commercial buildings, and visitor accommodation do not need assessing.

nodes.title: Activity and its risks
nodes.guidance: Describe the activity (e.g. 'Cultivation for winter crop') and each way it could harm freshwater (the pathway: sediment runoff, nitrogen leaching, direct stock access).

fields.label: How the activity is carried out

nodes.title: Significance of each risk by land unit
nodes.guidance: Rate each risk on each land unit as Minor, Moderate or Major (or Not applicable). The rating weighs the land unit's inherent vulnerability against how intensively it is farmed. Higher ratings need stronger or sooner actions. Schedule 7: make sure irrigation, nutrient and effluent application, stock exclusion from waterways, and offal and rubbish pits are all covered. Must cover: irrigation, nutrient application, effluent application, stock exclusion from waterways, offal pits, farm rubbish pits.

nodes.title: How risks were assessed
nodes.guidance: A short note on the method used to rate the risks (for example a vulnerability-by-intensity matrix).

parts.title: Action plan
parts.guidance: What you already do and what you will do to look after water, when each new thing will be done, and which land units it covers. An auditor checks that each action was done by its date, so set dates you can meet.

nodes.title: Action plan overview
nodes.guidance: A short summary of the main actions and why they were chosen.

nodes.title: Action table
nodes.guidance: One row per action. 'Existing' means you already do it; 'New' means you will start it within the next five years. Category: Regulated (needed to meet a rule, consent or regulation), Catchment (responds to the catchment's challenges and values), or Supplementary (anything else that reduces a risk).

fields.label: Records that will show it is done

parts.title: Maps
parts.guidance: The regulations list what the maps must show. Several items can share one map. Mark 'none on this farm' for anything that is not present rather than leaving it off.

nodes.title: Map: farm, land units and inherent vulnerabilities
nodes.guidance: Boundaries, land units, water and the natural features behind each land unit's vulnerabilities.

fields.label: Farm boundary, showing leased or licensed land
Land use areas (where uses are clearly distinct)
Potential intensive winter grazing areas and their critical source areas

nodes.title: Map: farming features
nodes.guidance: The farm infrastructure that relates to the risks and actions.

fields.label: Fencing that keeps stock out of waterbodies
Bores, surface water takes and intakes (with fish screens)
Stockholding areas (feed, winter, stand-off and loafing pads)
Other stock infrastructure (dairy shed, barns, yards)
Rubbish dumps, offal and silage pits, feed stores, agrichemical, fertiliser and fuel stores, washdown areas

nodes.title: Map: catchment information
nodes.guidance: Catchment features from the council's catchment context information that are relevant to this farm. Needed when the council holds relevant catchment context information.

nodes.title: Map: new physical works
nodes.guidance: Where each new physical work in the action plan will go (new fences, plantings, crossings). Needed when the action plan includes new physical works.

parts.title: Certification and audit record
parts.guidance: Filled in from what your certifier and auditor give you. Keep it current: it tells anyone reading the plan when it was certified, how the last audit went and when the next one is due.

nodes.title: Certification
nodes.guidance: Copy these from the certifier's decision. Needed when the plan has been certified.

nodes.title: Audits
nodes.guidance: One entry per audit, copied from the auditor's final report. Needed when the farm has been audited.

fields.label: Actions not implemented on time, and why

nodes.title: Evidence of actions done
nodes.guidance: Photos, invoices and notes that show each action was done. The regulations do not require you to keep these, but the auditor checks each action was done on time, so this is the easiest way to show it.

parts.title: Canterbury catchment context
parts.guidance: Canterbury detail that sits alongside the catchment context: the water zone, the regional plan rules that apply, and Ngāi Tahu values. ECan had not published freshwater farm plan catchment context information when this template was written; until it does, use the zone's implementation programme and the regional plan.

nodes.title: Water zone and regional plans
nodes.guidance: The Canterbury Water Management Strategy zone the farm is in, and the regional plans that apply (the Land and Water Regional Plan everywhere; the Hurunui and Waiau River Regional Plan or Waimakariri River Regional Plan as well where they apply).

nodes.title: Zone committee outcomes
nodes.guidance: The zone committee's vision and outcomes for water in this zone, and any targets in its implementation programme.

nodes.title: Ngāi Tahu values
nodes.guidance: Values, sites and mahinga kai important to the Papatipu Rūnanga for this area, with extracts from the iwi management plan that applies (for example the Mahaanui Iwi Management Plan in central Canterbury).

fields.label: Iwi management plan and sections referred to
Values and how the farm affects them

nodes.title: ECan catchment context information
nodes.guidance: Whether ECan has published catchment context, challenges and values information for this catchment, and the version used.

fields.label: Title and date of the information used

parts.title: Canterbury map layers
parts.guidance: Regional plan zones shown on the farm. These are the catchment features most Canterbury certifiers will expect to see.

nodes.title: Map: regional plan zones
nodes.guidance: Regional plan zones that cross or adjoin the farm.

fields.label: High Runoff Risk Phosphorus Zone
fields.guidance: LWRP planning maps; Sch 7 Pt B 2(g)

fields.label: Cultural Landscape/Values Management Area (Selwyn Te Waihora)

parts.title: Earlier farm environment plans
parts.guidance: If the farm had a Farm Environment Plan, its audit history helps the certifier. This part is for reference only.

nodes.title: FEP audit history
nodes.guidance: One row per earlier FEP audit.

fields.label: Rule or consent that required the FEP

parts.title: Schedule 7 property details
parts.guidance: The Schedule 7 property details that the national part does not already ask for.

nodes.title: Contact person
nodes.guidance: The named person ECan and the auditor contact about this plan.

nodes.title: Farm identifier
nodes.guidance: A farm identifier for the property, e.g. the ECan farm or Farm Portal identifier, a dairy supply number, or GPS coordinates of the farm entrance.

nodes.title: Responsibility for the plan
nodes.guidance: The person responsible for putting this plan into practice, and the owner's commitment. The auditor expects this person at the audit.

fields.label: Person responsible for implementing the plan

parts.title: Schedule 7 map items
parts.guidance: Schedule 7 map items not already covered by the national maps.

nodes.title: Map: Schedule 7 items
nodes.guidance: Can be shown on the farming features map instead of a separate map.

fields.label: Points on waterways where stock have access or cross
Riparian vegetation and fences next to waterbodies
Areas in or next to the farm shown in the District Plan as significant indigenous biodiversity
Land in the High Runoff Risk Phosphorus Zone
Flood protection or erosion control assets, including flood protection vegetation
Public access routes, or routes used to maintain rivers, streams or drains

parts.title: Nutrient budgets
parts.guidance: The farm's nutrient budget, prepared by a suitably qualified person in OverseerFM (or another model ECan has approved), with nitrogen baseline and current loss, and the Farm Portal report.

nodes.title: Nutrient budget and Farm Portal report
nodes.guidance: Copy these from the current nutrient budget and the Farm Portal report. Keep model versions together: never compare numbers from different Overseer versions.

fields.label: Good Management Practice Loss Rate (Farm Portal)

nodes.title: Nutrient budget by land management unit
nodes.guidance: Nitrogen and phosphorus loss for each land management unit, from the same budget.

parts.title: Management areas, objectives and targets
parts.guidance: Schedule 7 sets an objective and targets for seven management areas. For each target the plan must say how it will be met, in detail that matches the risk, the actions and good management practices with timeframes, and the records that will show it. Actions still to do go in the main action table, with the Schedule 7 target they serve.

nodes.title: 5A Nutrients
nodes.guidance: Fertiliser, nitrogen loss and phosphorus and sediment loss. Records usually include soil tests, fertiliser recommendations and application records, spreader calibration or Spreadmark certificates, proof of placement, and the current nutrient budget.

nodes.title: 5A Nutrients: Objective
nodes.guidance: The objective for this management area, in the plan's own words. Every target below serves it.
nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5A, Objective [S7a]
nodes.fixed_text: Use nutrients efficiently and minimise nutrient losses to water.

nodes.title: 5A Nutrients: Target 1
nodes.guidance: Say what you do to meet this target, in as much detail as the risk on this farm warrants, and which records show it. List any action still to do in the action table with a timeframe. Mark it Not applicable only if the activity does not happen on this farm, and say why.

fields.label: Practices in place and how the target is met
Records kept to show the target is met

nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5A, Target 1 [S7a]
nodes.fixed_text: Nitrogen losses from farming activities are at or below the: (a) Baseline GMP Loss Rate or Good Management Practice Loss Rate (whichever is the lesser); or (b) consented nitrogen loss limits.

nodes.title: 5A Nutrients: Target 2
nodes.guidance: Say what you do to meet this target, in as much detail as the risk on this farm warrants, and which records show it. List any action still to do in the action table with a timeframe. Mark it Not applicable only if the activity does not happen on this farm, and say why.

fields.label: Practices in place and how the target is met
Records kept to show the target is met

nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5A, Target 2 [S7a]
nodes.fixed_text: Available nitrogen loss mitigation measures (excluding those associated with irrigation, fertiliser or effluent management) are implemented.

nodes.title: 5A Nutrients: Target 3
nodes.guidance: Say what you do to meet this target, in as much detail as the risk on this farm warrants, and which records show it. List any action still to do in the action table with a timeframe. Mark it Not applicable only if the activity does not happen on this farm, and say why.

fields.label: Practices in place and how the target is met
Records kept to show the target is met

nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5A, Target 3 [S7a]
nodes.fixed_text: Phosphorus and sediment losses from farming activities are minimised.

nodes.title: 5A Nutrients: Target 4
nodes.guidance: Say what you do to meet this target, in as much detail as the risk on this farm warrants, and which records show it. List any action still to do in the action table with a timeframe. Mark it Not applicable only if the activity does not happen on this farm, and say why.

fields.label: Practices in place and how the target is met
Records kept to show the target is met

nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5A, Target 4 [S7a]
nodes.fixed_text: Manage the amount, timing and application of fertiliser inputs to match the predicted plant requirements and minimise nutrient losses.

nodes.title: 5A Nutrients: Target 5
nodes.guidance: Say what you do to meet this target, in as much detail as the risk on this farm warrants, and which records show it. List any action still to do in the action table with a timeframe. Mark it Not applicable only if the activity does not happen on this farm, and say why.

fields.label: Practices in place and how the target is met
Records kept to show the target is met

nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5A, Target 5 [S7a]
nodes.fixed_text: Store and load fertiliser to minimise the risk of spillage, leaching and loss into water bodies.

nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5A [S7a]

nodes.title: 5B Irrigation
nodes.guidance: Only where the farm irrigates. Records usually include design and commissioning reports for new systems, annual bucket or performance tests, maintenance records, soil moisture or water budget records, water meter data and staff training records. Switch this management area off when the farm does not irrigate.

nodes.title: 5B Irrigation: Objective
nodes.guidance: The objective for this management area, in the plan's own words. Every target below serves it.
nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5B, Objective [S7a]
nodes.fixed_text: The amount and timing of irrigation is managed to meet plant demands, minimise risk of leaching and runoff and ensure efficient water use.

nodes.title: 5B Irrigation: Target 1
nodes.guidance: Say what you do to meet this target, in as much detail as the risk on this farm warrants, and which records show it. List any action still to do in the action table with a timeframe. Mark it Not applicable only if the activity does not happen on this farm, and say why.

fields.label: Practices in place and how the target is met
Records kept to show the target is met

nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5B, Target 1 [S7a]
nodes.fixed_text: New irrigation systems are designed and installed in accordance with industry codes of practice and standards.

nodes.title: 5B Irrigation: Target 2
nodes.guidance: Say what you do to meet this target, in as much detail as the risk on this farm warrants, and which records show it. List any action still to do in the action table with a timeframe. Mark it Not applicable only if the activity does not happen on this farm, and say why.

fields.label: Practices in place and how the target is met
Records kept to show the target is met

nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5B, Target 2 [S7a]
nodes.fixed_text: The performance of irrigation systems is assessed annually and irrigation systems are maintained and operated to apply irrigation water at their optimal efficiency.

nodes.title: 5B Irrigation: Target 3
nodes.guidance: Say what you do to meet this target, in as much detail as the risk on this farm warrants, and which records show it. List any action still to do in the action table with a timeframe. Mark it Not applicable only if the activity does not happen on this farm, and say why.

fields.label: Practices in place and how the target is met

nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5B, Target 3 [S7a]
nodes.fixed_text: The timing and depth of irrigation water applied takes account of crop requirements and is justified through soil moisture monitoring or soil water budgets and climatic information.

nodes.title: 5B Irrigation: Target 4
nodes.guidance: Say what you do to meet this target, in as much detail as the risk on this farm warrants, and which records show it. List any action still to do in the action table with a timeframe. Mark it Not applicable only if the activity does not happen on this farm, and say why.

nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5B, Target 4 [S7a]
nodes.fixed_text: Staff are trained in the operation, maintenance and use of irrigation systems.

nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5B [S7a]

nodes.title: 5C Cultivation and soil structure
nodes.guidance: Cultivation, winter grazing and erosion. Records usually include cultivation and cropping records, the winter grazing plan and paddock selection, and maps of erosion-prone areas and critical source areas.

nodes.title: 5C Cultivation and soil structure: Objective
nodes.guidance: The objective for this management area, in the plan's own words. Every target below serves it.
nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5C, Objective [S7a]
nodes.fixed_text: The physical and biological condition of soils is maintained or improved in order to minimise the movement of sediment, phosphorus and other contaminants to waterways.

nodes.title: 5C Cultivation and soil structure: Target 1
nodes.guidance: Say what you do to meet this target, in as much detail as the risk on this farm warrants, and which records show it. List any action still to do in the action table with a timeframe. Mark it Not applicable only if the activity does not happen on this farm, and say why.

fields.label: Practices in place and how the target is met

nodes.fixed_text: Farming activities are managed so as to not exacerbate erosion.

nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5C, Target 2 [S7a]
nodes.fixed_text: Farming practices are implemented that optimise infiltration of water into the soil profile and minimise run-off of water, sediment loss and erosion.

nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5C [S7a]

nodes.title: 5D Animal effluent and solid animal waste
nodes.guidance: Where effluent or solid animal waste is collected and applied. Records usually include the effluent discharge area map, application records, storage calculations, design certificates, backflow preventer checks and staff training. Switch this management area off when no animal effluent or solid animal waste is collected.

nodes.title: 5D Animal effluent and solid animal waste: Objective
nodes.guidance: The objective for this management area, in the plan's own words. Every target below serves it.
nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5D, Objective [S7a]
nodes.fixed_text: Animal effluent and solid animal waste is managed to minimise nutrient leaching and run-off.

nodes.title: 5D Animal effluent and solid animal waste: Target 1
nodes.guidance: Say what you do to meet this target, in as much detail as the risk on this farm warrants, and which records show it. List any action still to do in the action table with a timeframe. Mark it Not applicable only if the activity does not happen on this farm, and say why.

fields.label: Practices in place and how the target is met
Records kept to show the target is met

nodes.cite: LWRP Schedule 7 Part B item 5D, Target 1 [S7a]

parts.title: Farm Environment Plan audits
parts.guidance: Schedule 7 plans are audited by an ECan Certified Farm Environment Plan Auditor who is independent of the farm and did not help write the plan. The auditor grades the plan A to D; the grade sets when the next audit is due under the consent or rule.
